questions.question: Does the self-healing (Zr,Hf)O2 crack-filling mechanism in silicide coatings on HfNbTaTiZr remain effective if the alloy oxygen content drops below 1.0 wt.%, and how does this threshold affect the parabolic oxidation rate constant?
questions.rationale: The paper links high strength and a specific self-healing oxidation mechanism to the presence of ~1.0 wt.% oxygen. Reducing oxygen to mitigate embrittlement could disable the (Zr,Hf)O2 healing mechanism, necessitating a new boundary for acceptable oxygen levels.
questions.decision_use: Determines if oxygen levels can be safely lowered to improve ductility without sacrificing the oxidation resistance provided by the specific self-healing mechanism.
answer_requirements: Measure parabolic oxidation rate constants for HfNbTaTiZr silicide-coated samples with systematically varied oxygen contents (0.2 to 1.0 wt.%)
Perform high-temperature microstructural analysis to observe the presence and continuity of (Zr,Hf)O2 phases in the oxide scale
evidence_spans: This is explained by the formation of (Zr,Hf)O 2 filling cracks within the silicide layer and protecting the underlying alloy by expelling Si under the cracks.

questions.question: Is the parabolic oxidation rate constant of 0.80 mg^2 cm^-4 h^-1 for silicide-coated HfNbTaTiZr maintained under cyclic thermal loading (flame testing) at temperatures exceeding 1200 °C, or does the (Zr,Hf)O2 sealant degrade over time?
questions.rationale: The reported low rate constant is from static or limited testing. High-temperature applications involve thermal cycling. Knowing if the (Zr,Hf)O2 sealant remains intact under cyclic stress is necessary to validate the coating for real-world service.
questions.decision_use: Validates the long-term viability of the silicide coating strategy for cyclic high-temperature service versus single-use or static applications.
answer_requirements: Conduct cyclic oxidation tests at high temperatures (>1200 °C) for extended durations
Measure mass change kinetics per cycle and perform cross-sectional SEM to assess the integrity of the (Zr,Hf)O2 sealant
